Hi Rania — thanks for sending these over and for the sample Fatoora. I pulled the PO hold reason from Procurement: we need a couple of Saudi-specific items before we can move the vendor to ‘Active’ and issue the PO for payment routing. Please see the checklist below and tick what you can provide this week: 

Required for PO activation (minimum):
- Commercial Registration (CR) — received (good)
- ZATCA e-invoice sample in Fatoora/Fattoura format — received (looks ok; need one more)
- Signed vendor onboarding form including legal entity and remittance details — received (thanks)
- Confirmation of VAT registration number (VAT ID) or statement that supplier is non-resident for VAT purposes
- Certificate of Tax Residency (CTR) or equivalent for reverse-charge claims (if you expect the PO to be treated as reverse-charge)
- Bank details (IBAN, SWIFT, account holder as appears on CR) and a bank confirmation letter for cross-border wires

Optional but helpful:
- Sample invoice using your Fatoora XML with the tax fields populated (we'll validate mapping)
- Any local fiscal representative details if you use a fiscal agent in KSA

Answers to your questions:
- For non-resident suppliers providing digital/marketing/consulting services, Redwood typically self-assesses VAT under the reverse-charge mechanism only when the supplier confirms non-resident status and provides appropriate residency evidence; otherwise ZATCA rules may require collection of VAT at source.
- We generally ask for a Certificate of Tax Residency to support reverse-charge treatment. Our Tax team will review and confirm on a per-invoice basis.
- For wire instructions: we accept both cross-border (IBAN/SWIFT) and local SAR clearing (if you provide a local bank account); please indicate preferred remittance currency.

Next steps: If you can send the CTR and one populated Fatoora invoice, I will escalate to Finance this week to remove the PO hold. If any of those items are delayed, confirm and we'll evaluate interim workarounds.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Senior Procurement Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rania — received the populated Fatoora and CTR. I validated the XML payload quickly with our integration engineer; two small gaps on mapping (we'll send field notes) but nothing blocking.

On your two clarifying points:
- Split-scope approach: Procurement prefers you submit two invoice line groups under the same PO where possible (Group A: local media with VAT applied; Group B: consulting/services flagged as non-resident supply for reverse-charge). Finance can accept one consolidated invoice as long as VAT treatment is explicit per line and supporting CTR is referenced. If it simplifies your billing, separate invoices (one SAR local VAT, one USD consulting) are also OK — specify the Redwood entity on each invoice.
- Mixed currency: We can accept mixed-currency POs but Finance will prefer clear currency-coded lines and a single payment instruction for each currency. SAR settlement is fine for local publisher passes-through; mark the invoice with the SAR account details and use our PO reference.

Action plan:
1) Ben — can you confirm Finance signoff for the CTR as residency evidence for reverse-charge? If yes, we can clear the PO hold pending the small XML mapping fixes.
2) Laura — I need the PO number assigned once Finance confirms the CTR.

Rania, we'll follow up with the exact XML field mapping within 24 hours. If you can re-send the populated Fatoora with amounts and the final preferred currency approach, we will expedite.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Procurement Lead, Redwood Inference
